questions.question: The first and the easiest part of concept evaluation is called the full screen.
questions.explanation: The second and the more rigorous part of concept evaluation is called the full screen. The term "full" here means that one now has as much information as one is going to get before undertaking technical work on the product.

questions.question: The full screen conducted for a concept identifies the feasibility of technical accomplishment and feasibility of commercial accomplishment of the concept.
questions.explanation: Feasibility of technical accomplishment and feasibility of commercial accomplishment, often through a scoring model, is central to most full screens.

questions.question: If a concept passes the full screen, the next phase in the new products process is the product launch phase.
questions.explanation: If a concept passes the full screen, the next phase in the new products process is development. The concept will become a new product development project and will require a serious increase in commitment of financial and human resources.

questions.question: Concepts that pass the full screen are "rank-ordered" by attractiveness so that the firm has some options on standby when an ongoing project stalls or is canceled.
questions.explanation: The best of the concepts through the full screen can be rank ordered or prioritized such that one has some options on standby when an ongoing project stalls or is canceled, while unacceptable, but possibly worthwhile, concepts get cycled back into concept development where more work may make them acceptable.

questions.question: A full-screen discourages cross-functional communication.
questions.explanation: The full screen encourages cross-functional communication. It flushes out all basic disagreements about a project and sets them up for discussion. These disagreements put the spotlight on "potholes" or hurdles that the concept will face during development and show where new people may be needed.

questions.question: The list of factors used in the scoring model for the full screen should be reduced as much as possible and always kept fluid.
questions.explanation: In general, a firm should start with the list of factors that includes technical task difficulty, rate of technological change, design superiority assistance and so on and scratch out any that clearly is not applicable, insert any obviously omitted, and then use it for a few times to see how the scores set with the people involved. Over time the list should be reduced as much as possible and always kept fluid.

questions.question: Raw materials or components supply is one of the technical success factors included in the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model.
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 8.5. Technical success factors include manufacturing capability, technical complexity, and proprietary position, while commercial success factors include raw materials or components supply, customer strength, channels to market, and customer or market need.

questions.question: Customer strength is one of the commercial success factors in the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model.
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 8.5. In the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model, technical success factors include manufacturing capability, technical complexity, and proprietary position, while commercial success factors include customer strength, channels to market, and customer or market need.

questions.question: A key role for the product innovation charter is to point out exclusions that are sometimes called culling factors.
questions.explanation: A key role for the product innovation charter is to point out exclusions that are sometimes called culling factors.

questions.question: Scoring models are advantageous because of their use of weights as the weightings are not judgmental.
questions.explanation: The most serious criticism of scoring models is their use of weights because the weightings are necessarily judgmental. Because of weighting's importance, some firms measure its effect using sensitivity testing. Scoring models are actually just mathematical models or equations, so an analyst can alter the scorings or the weightings to see what difference the alterations make in the final score.

questions.question: The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is a purely statistical technique used to identify the correlation of specified factors with past successes and failures.
questions.explanation: The Analytic Hierarchy Process, developed in the 1970s by Thomas Saaty, is a general technique that systematically gathers expert judgment and uses it to make optimal decisions. It has been used in dozens of business and nonbusiness settings over the years and can be applied in full screening as a way to prioritize and select new product projects.

questions.question: When used as a full screen technique, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) gathers managerial judgment and expertise to identify the key criteria in the screening decision.
questions.explanation: When used as a full screen technique, AHP gathers managerial judgment and expertise to identify the key criteria in the screening decision, obtain scores for each project under consideration relative to these criteria, and rank the projects in order of desirability. Commercially available software such as Expert Choice makes AHP very easy to use.

questions.question: The full screen is used as part of concept evaluation to:
choices: A. develop the product innovation charter.
B. help the firm decide whether it should go forward with the concept or quit.
C. plan the process of product launch.
D. help the firm analyze the technical aspects of its competitors' products.
questions.explanation: The full screen helps the firm decide whether it should go forward with the concept or quit. Keep in mind that if a concept passes the full screen, the next phase in the new products process is development.

questions.question: The primary purpose of the full screen is to:
choices: A. estimate the feasibility of technical and commercial accomplishments.
B. finalize the overall marketing plan for the product.
C. develop and test a prototype of the product.
D. obtain the information required for developing the product innovation charter.
questions.explanation: Feasibility of technical accomplishment and feasibility of commercial accomplishment are often assessed using the full screen through a scoring model. This is central to most full screens.

questions.question: If a concept passes the full screen, _____.
choices: A. it enters the concept development stage
B. the next phase in the new products process is development
C. the product innovation charter for the concept is developed
questions.explanation: If a concept passes the full screen, the next phase in the new products process is development. The concept will become a new product development project and will require a serious increase in commitment of financial and human resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to help managers in screening hundreds or even thousands of new product concepts in a year?
choices: A. Reinventing the wheel when a concept similar to one that has been rejected comes up again later
B. Bypassing the full screen to begin technical development
C. Maintaining a record of rejected concepts
D. Cancelling concepts that are unacceptable, but possibly worthwhile
questions.explanation: A record is kept of rejected concepts to prevent reinventing the wheel when a similar concept comes up again later. This may seem like a trivial point, but to managers who screen hundreds or even thousands of new product concepts a year, it is not trivial. A good corporate memory helps settle arguments later.

questions.question: Which of the following is an objective of full screening?
choices: A. To add the thoughts of potential users to the set of market data collected
B. To provide data for the product innovation charter
questions.explanation: The full screen encourages cross-functional communication. It flushes out all basic disagreements about a project (including the ever-present politics) and sets them up for discussion. These disagreements put the spotlight on "potholes" or hurdles that the concept will face during development and show where new people may be needed.

questions.question: Those firms that bypass the full screen:
choices: A. are generally larger in size.
B. are generally involved with new product work.
C. tend to have a highly technical development process.
D. are more likely to do a more complete concept test.
questions.explanation: Some firms bypass the full screen. Smaller firms not doing much new product work may prefer what really is an opinion poll where one or more people make a judgment on some informal checklist. Some packaged goods firms whose development process is rather nontechnical also may skip the full screen. To compensate for a lack of a full screen, these firms may do a more complete concept test and what they call premarket testing sales forecasting models.

questions.question: Which of the following firms is most likely to employ a formal full screening of product concepts?
choices: A. A small firm that is not involved in much new product work
B. A packaged goods firm whose development process is rather nontechnical
C. A firm that has the ability to market its product and is aware of the technical feasibility of its products
D. A firm that is facing major issues of technical feasibility in the new product development process
questions.explanation: When technical feasibility and a firm's ability to market a product are not known, the full screen is conducted. Some packaged goods firms whose development process is rather nontechnical (me-too products and simple variations on what is already on the market) may skip the full screen. Smaller firms not doing much new product work may prefer what really is an opinion poll where one or more people make a judgment on some informal checklist.

questions.question: A single best factor on which the scoring model can be based and which covers both technical and commercial accomplishments and considers all direct and indirect costs and benefits can be termed as the _____.
questions.explanation: With reference to the scoring model, there is one factor that covers both technical and commercial accomplishment, a financial term called net present value of the discounted stream of earnings from the product concept, considering all direct and indirect costs and benefits.

questions.question: The estimation of the likelihood of commercial accomplishment during the screening procedure of the scoring model assesses:
choices: A. whether the firm can create something that will do what its customers want.
B. whether the firm has the resources to develop the product.
C. whether product prototypes can be used to judge real-time market expenses.
D. whether a product can be sold profitably.
questions.explanation: The overall value of the concept is assessed by estimating the likelihood of technical accomplishment (whether one can create something that will do what customers want) and the likelihood of commercial accomplishment (whether one can sell it profitably). That is, "can we make it," and "will they buy it?"

questions.question: Which of the following is a technical success factor of the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model?
choices: B. Raw materials or components supply
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 8.5. The technical success factors of the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model include proprietary position, competencies or skills, technical complexity, access to and effective use of external technology, and manufacturing capability.

questions.question: Which of the following methods of combining an individual team member's ratings involves dropping the highest and lowest ratings before averaging?
questions.explanation: Various methods are used to combine the individual team member's ratings, an average (mean) being the most common. Some firms use the Olympic figure-skating method of dropping the highest and lowest ratings before averaging.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be a commercial success factor by the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model?
choices: B. Raw materials or components supply
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 8.5. The technical success factors of the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model include proprietary position, competencies, access to and effective use of external technology. Commercial success factors, on the other hand, include safety, health, environmental risks, customer strength, brand recognition, and so on.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common means of combining the ratings of individual team members in a full screening project?
questions.explanation: Various methods are used to combine the individual team member's ratings, an average (mean) being the most common. Some firms use the Olympic figure-skating method of dropping the highest and lowest ratings before averaging. Some firms have an open discussion after the averages are shown, so individuals can make a case for any view that is at odds with the group.

questions.question: Star Inc. has restricted its budget for developing new products to $20,000. It automatically vetoes a proposed product if the product scores poorly on the factor of budget during the screening process. In this case, such a factor is known as a _____ factor.
questions.explanation: In this case, such a factor is known as a culling factor. On some factors, a bad score constitutes a veto. For example, in the case of the student seeking to decide what entertainment to pursue this weekend, a money shortage may block anything costing more than $30. This problem should be faced in the beginning so no time is wasted drumming up options costing more than $30. Industry is the same, and a key role for the product innovation charter is to point out those exclusions. These are sometimes called culling factors.

questions.question: In the context of the scoring model, culling factors should generally be established in the _____.
questions.explanation: On some factors, a bad score constitutes a veto. For example, in the case of the student seeking to decide what entertainment to pursue this weekend, a money shortage may block anything costing more than $30. This problem should be faced in the beginning so no time is wasted drumming up options costing more than $30. Industry is the same, and a key role for the product innovation charter is to point out those exclusions. These are sometimes called culling factors.

questions.question: Comport Corp. automatically dismisses any concept that does not seem to have the potential to be first or second in its market. In this case, Comport is using market share as a _____.
questions.explanation: In this case, Comport is using market share as a culling factor. Factors that point out to exclusions or indicate projects that cannot be taken further are known as culling factors. A key role for the product innovation charter is to point out these exclusions.

questions.question: When combining the individual team member's ratings, if the factors being scored have all-or-nothing, yes-or-no answers, then these factors should be handled by using:
choices: A. benefit segmentation for the given factors.
B. the end points on the semantic differential scale, with no gradations.
C. the Olympic method of dropping the highest and lowest ratings.
D. the risk-payoff model of factor screening.
questions.explanation: A problem occurs when the factor being scored has all-or-nothing, yes-or no answers; for example, "Will this concept require the establishment of a separate sales force?" This type of factor is handled by using the end points on the semantic differential scale, with no gradations.

questions.question: Who among the following is less likely to be a member of the scoring team for a full screening process in an organization?
questions.explanation: Selecting the members of a scoring team is like selecting the members of a new products team. Top business unit managers (presidents, general managers) should stay out of the act, except, of course, in small firms. Such people inhibit the frank discussions needed when assessing the firm's capabilities. The four major functions (marketing, technical, operations, and finance) are involved, as are new products managers and staff specialists from information technology, distribution, procurement, public relations, human resources, and so on, depending on the firm's procedure for developing new products.

questions.question: Since factor weightings are of great importance, many firms evaluate the impact of assigned weights through _____.
questions.explanation: Because of weighting's importance, some firms measure its effect using sensitivity testing. Scoring models are actually just mathematical models or equations, so an analyst can alter the scorings or the weightings to see what difference the alterations make in the final score.

questions.question: The use of weights in scoring models is subject to serious criticism because:
choices: B. the effect of weightings cannot be measured using sensitivity analysis.
C. they use all-or-nothing, yes-or-no answers as factors.
D. they can be used only for open-ended questions.
questions.explanation: The most serious criticism of scoring models is their use of weights because the weightings are necessarily judgmental. Because of weighting's importance, some firms measure its effect using sensitivity testing. Scoring models are actually just mathematical models or equations, so an analyst can alter the scorings or the weightings to see what difference the alterations make in the final score.

questions.question: Valclick Inc., during the full screen phase of its new product process, uses an approach that graphically arranges five-point scorings on different factors. Which of the following approaches is Valclick using in this scenario?
questions.explanation: An alternative preferred by some firms for its graphic capability for scoring is called the profile sheet. The profile sheet graphically arranges the five-point scorings on the different factors. If a team of judges is used, the profile employs average scores.

questions.question: Which of the following techniques is most likely to be used for product project screening and evaluation?
questions.explanation: One of the techniques for product project screening and evaluation is the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). AHP, developed in the 1970s by Thomas Saaty, is a general technique that systematically gathers expert judgment and uses it to make optimal decisions.

questions.question: The Analytic Hierarchy Process is a form of _____ analysis.
questions.explanation: One of the techniques for product project screening and evaluation is the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). It uses a hierarchical decision tree. The tree will show a manager's ultimate goal (in this case, choosing the best new product project) at the top. The next level below will include all the primary criteria the manager considers important in reaching the goal. There may be several levels of criteria (secondary, tertiary, etc.) under the primary criteria in the tree. Lastly, the choices (new product projects under consideration) are placed at the bottom of the tree.

questions.question: _____ is a commercially available software that makes the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) very easy to use.
questions.explanation: When used as a full screen technique, AHP gathers managerial judgment and expertise to identify the key criteria in the screening decision, obtains scores for each project under consideration relative to these criteria, and ranks the projects in order of desirability. Commercially available software such as Expert Choice makes AHP very easy to use.

questions.question: Lia Hwang was asked to attend a new product scoring session in order to explain the special considerations and the intangible benefits unique to the concept she helped develop. Lia's role was to push past normal resistance to change and to see that the concept gets a fair hearing at all turns. Lia is best described as a _____.
questions.explanation: Lia is a product champion since product champions are needed to push past normal resistance to change and to see that the concept gets a fair hearing at all turns. They try to give the scorers all favorable information and may argue that standard forms don't fit their special situations.

questions.question: Which of the following techniques can be used by a product champion to ensure that the concept gets a fair hearing at all turns?
choices: A. By deciding the weights for the factors included in a scoring model
B. By selecting an appropriate scoring model
D. By providing all favorable information
questions.explanation: Product champions are sometimes needed to push past normal resistance to change and to see that the concept gets a fair hearing at all turns. They try to give the scorers all favorable information and may argue that standard forms don't fit their special situations.

questions.question: The full screen often involves the use of a _____, which is an arrangement of checklist factors with weights (importances) on them.
questions.explanation: The second and the more rigorous part of concept evaluation is called the full screen. The term "full" here means that one now has as much information as one is going to get before undertaking technical work on the product. The full screen often involves the use of a scoring model, which is an arrangement of checklist factors with weights (importances) on them.

questions.question: The hierarchical decision tree in the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) will show the manager's ultimate goal at the top. The next level below will include:
choices: A. all the primary criteria the manager considers important in reaching the goal.
B. all the secondary criteria the manager considers important in reaching the goal.
C. new product projects under consideration.
D. projects that had been rejected in the recent past.
questions.explanation: The hierarchical decision tree in the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) will show the manager's ultimate goal at the top. The next level below will include all the primary criteria the manager considers important in reaching the goal. There may be several levels of criteria (secondary, tertiary, etc.) under the primary criteria in the tree. Lastly, the choices (new product projects under consideration) are placed at the bottom of the tree.

questions.question: Discuss the objectives of full screen.
questions.answer:
The full screen accomplishes three essential objectives:

• It helps a firm decide whether it should go forward with a concept or quit. The concept will become a new product development project and will require a serious increase in commitment of financial and human resources. The full screen helps one decide whether these resources should be devoted to the project and, if so, how vigorously.
• It helps manage the process by sorting the concepts and identifying the best ones. The best of the concepts can be rank ordered or prioritized such that one has some options on standby when an ongoing project stalls or is canceled.
• It encourages cross-functional communication. The screening process is a learning process, particularly in making managers more sensitive to how other functions think. It flushes out all basic disagreements about a project and sets them up for discussion. These disagreements put the spotlight on hurdles that the concept will face during development and show where new people may be needed.

questions.question: Briefly discuss the technical and commercial success factors included in the Industrial Research Institute Scoring Model.
questions.answer:
The technical success factors include the following:

• Proprietary Position: Developing a strong, defendable patent in the technology to be researched.
• Competencies/Skills: Available technical resources have the competencies to undertake the research project.
• Technical Complexity: The impact of technical complexity on product success.
• Access to and Effective Use of External Technology: The availability of external technology and the firm's ability to use it successfully.
• Manufacturing Capability: Relates to whether the firm has internal or external capabilities to manufacture the product or incorporate the process into its operations.
The commercial success factors include the following:
• Customer/Market Need: Is there a ready market for the product or the process, resulting from the project?
• Market/Brand Recognition: The likelihood that the product will be accepted in the marketplace, due to company strengths and/or image.
• Channels to Market: The ease with which the product will be introduced and distributed.
• Customer Strength: The probability that the product will succeed or fail based upon the strength of the customer in the business area of interest.
• Raw Materials/Components Supply: The effect of the availability of key components and materials.
• Safety, Health, and Environmental Risks: The probability that any of these effects will hinder project success.

questions.question: Discuss the role of individuals as scorers or judges in a scoring model.
questions.answer: Selecting the members of a scoring team is like selecting the members of a new products team. The four major functions (marketing, technical, operations, and finance) are involved, as are new products managers and staff specialists from information technology, distribution, procurement, public relations, human resources, and so on, depending on the firm's procedure for developing new products. Problems with individuals are more specific. Research indicates that (1) some people are always optimistic, (2) some are sometimes optimistic and sometimes pessimistic, (3) some are "neutrals" who score to the middle of scales, (4) some are far more reliable and accurate than others, (5) some are easily swayed by the group, and (6) some are capable but erratic. Scoring teams need a manager to deal with such problems. Some firms actually weight each evaluator's scores by past accuracy (defined as conformity with the team's scores). Dow Brands uses a computerized groupware approach primarily because they like the scorings to be anonymous.

questions.question: Explain the analytic hierarchy process.
questions.answer: The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is a technique for product project screening and evaluation. AHP, developed in the 1970s by Thomas Saaty, is a general technique that systematically gathers expert judgment and uses it to make optimal decisions. The product manager begins by building a hierarchical decision tree. The tree will show the manager's ultimate goal at the top. The next level below will include all the primary criteria the manager considers important in reaching the goal. There may be several levels of criteria under the primary criteria in the tree. Lastly, the choices are placed at the bottom of the tree. Next, the manager provides comparison data for each element in the tree with respect to the next higher level. The AHP software takes over from this point. It converts the comparison data into a set of relative weights, which are then aggregated to obtain composite priorities of each element at each level. Ultimately, the available choices are rank ordered in terms of their preferability to the manager.

questions.question: The evaluation process begins with the creation of a prototype.
questions.explanation: The new product appears first as an idea, a concept in words or pictures, and that is evaluated first.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: If a firm makes products with very long cycle times, it is required to control the number of products it has in the process queue at any given time so that products receive development funds in a timely manner.
questions.explanation: If a firm makes products with very short cycle times, such as computer games, it has to control the number of products it has in the process queue at any given time so that products receive development funds in a timely manner.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: The late expenditures curve is representative of product development in technical fields such as optics.
questions.explanation: The early expenditures curve is representative of product development in technical fields, such as pharmaceuticals, optics, and computers. R&D is the big part of the cost package, and marketing costs are relatively small.

questions.question: With reference to the risk/payoff matrix, a "drop error" occurs when a product, that is likely to fail if marketed, is continued.
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 7.3. The decision to stop a project when it would actually succeed leads to the occurrence of a "drop error."

questions.question: A "go error" and a "drop error" have the same cost and probability dimensions.
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 7.3. A "drop error" is much worse than a "go error" and both of them differ in terms of cost and probability dimensions.

questions.question: A firm that develops a contingency plan prior to launching a new product is adopting an active acceptance risk strategy.
questions.explanation: In general, a new products team should consider four generic risk strategies. Developing a contingency plan is active acceptance and passive acceptance is to deal with the risks as they come up.

questions.question: The perceptual map analysis leads to the idea of a decay curve.
questions.explanation: The risk matrix decisions lead to the idea of a decay curve. By applying the new products process, the hundreds or thousands of ideas the company may have started with gradually get reduced.

questions.question: In new product work, financial analysis should be done by firms as early as possible to avoid wasting money on poor projects.
questions.explanation: A fallacy related to new product work is that financial analysis should be done as early as possible to avoid wasting money on poor projects. This philosophy leads firms to make complex financial analysis shortly after early concept testing, although the numbers are inadequate.

questions.question: Concept testing is different from concept development as it undermines the idea of helping an item and kills it off.
questions.explanation: An evaluation system should contain early testing that is supportive. In fact, concept testing is sometimes called concept development to reinforce the idea of helping the item, not just killing it off.

questions.question: Surrogate questions help when the timing of factual information does not often match one's need for it.
questions.explanation: The timing of factual information does not often match ones' need for it. For example, one wants to know customer reactions early on, even before the product is developed.

questions.question: The A-T-A-R concept is based on the diffusion of risk model.
questions.explanation: The A-T-A-R concept is taken from what is called diffusion of innovation, explained this way: For a person or a firm to become a regular buyer/user of an innovation, there must first be awareness that it exists, then there must be a decision to try that innovation, then the person must find the item available to them, and finally there must be the type of happiness with it that leads to adoption, or repeat usage.

questions.question: A-T-A-R is a term that came from consumer products marketing.
questions.explanation: A-T-A-R is a term that came from consumer products marketing. Industry has traditionally used slightly different language, so a natural question is, "Does the model apply to all types of new products, including industrial ones, and services too?" The answer is absolutely, though each term may be defined slightly differently in different settings.

questions.question: A-T-A-R is a term that came from consumer products marketing.
questions.explanation: A-T-A-R is a term that came from consumer products marketing. Industry has traditionally used slightly different language, so a natural question is whether the model applies to all types of new products, including industrial ones, and services too. The answer is absolutely, though each term may be defined slightly differently in different settings.

questions.question: The product innovation charter (PIC) directing new product development eliminates more product ideas than all the other evaluations combined.
questions.explanation: The earliest evaluation that a firm makes is of itself and its situation and yields "a priori" conclusions about new product proposals is called the product innovation charter. The charter given to new products management eliminates many product ideas.
questions.topic: Concept Evaluation: Fit with Product Innovation Charter

questions.question: The earliest evaluation that a firm makes is of itself and its situation, which yields a priori conclusions about new product proposals.
questions.explanation: The earliest evaluation that a firm makes is of itself and its situation. That evaluation yields a priori conclusions about new product proposals. The firm reaches these conclusions while making basic strategic decisions on the product innovation charter (PIC).
questions.topic: Concept Evaluation: Fit with Product Innovation Charter

questions.question: A complete new product concept is a statement about anticipated product features that will yield problem solutions relative to other products already available.
questions.explanation: A complete new product concept is a statement about anticipated product features (form or technology) that will yield selected benefits or problem solutions relative to other products already available.

questions.question: The first purpose of a concept test is to generate the sales or trial rate that a product would enjoy.
questions.explanation: The first purpose of a concept test is to identify very poor concepts so that they can be eliminated. If music lovers, for example, don't care about a new kind of compact disc that will last forever (because they download all their music from online sources) and thus reject it out of hand, the concept is probably a poor one.

questions.question: Concept testing can be used for developing an idea, not just for testing it.
questions.explanation: The third purpose of concept testing is to help develop an idea, not just test it. Concepts rarely emerge from a test the way they went in.

questions.question: Prototypes are the least expensive form of concept statements because very few decisions have to be made about the new product to get it into a prototype.
questions.explanation: Prototypes, or models, are a third, more expensive form of concept statement because many decisions have to be made about the new product to get it into a prototype.

questions.question: Virtual reality captures the advantages and all the disadvantages of a prototype.
questions.explanation: Virtual reality is a type of concept format that captures the advantages of a prototype without most of the disadvantages.

questions.question: Benefit segmentation is used to identify unsatisfied market segments and concentrate a firm's efforts on developing concepts ideally suited to the needs of those segments.
questions.explanation: Through benefit segmentation, a firm may identify unsatisfied market segments and concentrate its efforts on developing concepts ideally suited to the needs of these segments.

questions.question: If the number of determinant attributes is very less, identifying benefit segments on an importance map can be very complex.
questions.explanation: Suppose there are only two attributes to consider, it might be very simple to identify benefit segments on an importance map.

questions.question: When benefit segments are overlaid onto a perceptual map, it results in a cumulative expenditures curve.
questions.explanation: Overlaying the benefit segments onto a perceptual map results in what is called a joint space map. It allows one to assess the preferences of each benefit segment for different product concepts.

questions.question: A new product appears first as a(n) _____.
questions.explanation: A new product appears first as an idea, a concept in words or pictures. As workers turn the concept into a formed piece of metal, or software, or a new factory site preparation service, that good or service is then evaluated.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: Which of the following actions causes backtracking?
choices: A. When the product development process is carried out step by step
B. When the costs of incomplete product development are higher than the costs of delayed introduction
C. When an idea or concept cannot be implemented until after a prototype has been created
D. When the steps in the product development process are skipped
questions.explanation: There was an era when a new product's development happened step by step, nothing ahead of its time. But today one may be working on a package before one has actually finished the product. This often causes backtracking.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: The very first evaluation in the product development process usually:
choices: A. occurs after a product idea has been developed.
C. follows the development of a prototype.
questions.explanation: During the evaluation process, ideas become concepts; concepts get refined, evaluated, and approved; development projects are initiated; and products are launched. Throughout this process, different questions need to be asked, and different evaluation techniques provide the required answers. The very first evaluation precedes the product concept—in fact, it takes place in Phase I of the basic new products process, when an opportunity or threat is identified and assessed.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: The first use of evaluation is focused upon:
choices: A. the development of a marketing plan.
B. the likely success of the product concept that has been selected for development.
C. mistakes made during the launch of the new product.
D. providing direction for the selection of potential product concepts.
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 7.1. The very first evaluation precedes the product concept—in fact, it takes place in Phase I of the basic new products process, when an opportunity or threat is identified and assessed. This early evaluation step (direction) is shown to indicate where one should look, and what one should try to exploit, and what one should fight against. Throughout the evaluation process, different questions need to be asked, and different evaluation techniques provide the required answers.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: During the concept generation phase of the basic new products process, the goal of product evaluation is to:
choices: B. cull out the big/sure losers.
C. conduct protocol checks and prototype tests.
questions.explanation: Evaluation tasks change as one progresses through the basic new product process. In Phase II of the new products process, which is concept generation, ideas begin to appear, and the purpose of evaluation changes: The goal is to avoid the big loser or the sure loser.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: With reference to the purpose of evaluation, which of the following questions that a firm asks, tests the aspect of scalability of assessing ideas in the concept generation phase of the basic new products process?
choices: A. Does it meet a specific customer need?
B. Does the firm have the capability to develop and launch the idea?
C. Can the firm become more efficient in production as volume increases?
D. Is there a good match corporate strategy and culture?
questions.explanation: The question, "Can the firm become more efficient in production as volume increases?" tests the aspect of scalability of assessing ideas in the concept generation phase of the basic new products process.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: The primary purpose of evaluation during Phase III of the basic new products process is to:
choices: B. create a final, full-scale prototype.
C. identify concepts that will proceed further in the development process.
D. eliminate all probable mistakes in the launch phase.
questions.explanation: At the concept evaluation phase of the basic new products process, the purpose of evaluation concerns the decision of sending the concept into full-scale development. This decision, if the amounts to be spent make it an important decision, will benefit from a very thorough scoring model application.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: A _____ is an evaluation technique that tells one whether he or she is ready to develop a product for serious field testing.
questions.explanation: A protocol check tells one whether he or she is ready to develop a product for serious field testing.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: The evaluation issue during the launch phase in the new product development process that seeks to find out if a firm has proven itself able to make and market an item on a commercial scale is usually carried out by the evaluation task called _____.
questions.explanation: In Phase V of the basic new products process, the attention turns to launching an item. The evaluation issue now is whether the firm has proven itself able to make, and market, the item on a commercial scale. This is usually resolved by some form of market testing.
questions.topic: What's Going On in the New Products Process?

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true of the cumulative expenditure curve?
choices: A. The early expenditures curve initially slopes downward and then starts sloping upward.
B. The late expenditures curve is representative of product development in technical fields such as optics.
C. The late expenditures curve initially slopes upward and then starts sloping downward.
D. The early expenditures curve is representative of product development in technical fields.
questions.explanation: The early expenditures curve is representative of product development in technical fields, such as pharmaceuticals, optics, and computers. R&D is the big part of the cost package, and marketing costs are relatively small. The lower curve that indicates late expenditures shows the opposite type of firm, say, a consumer packaged goods company. Here the technical expenditures may be small, but a huge TV advertising program is needed at introduction.

questions.question: Which of the following industries is most likely to be represented by a late expenditures curve?
questions.explanation: The early expenditures curve is representative of product development in technical fields, such as pharmaceuticals, optics, and computers. R&D is the big part of the cost package, and marketing costs are relatively small. The lower curve shows the opposite type of firm, say, a consumer packaged goods company. Here the technical expenditures may be small, but a huge TV advertising program is needed at introduction.

questions.question: Which of the following outcomes of a risk/payoff matrix, used for evaluating a new product process, is most likely to be the costliest for a firm?
choices: A. Stopping a product that is likely to fail
B. Continuing a product that is likely to fail
C. Stopping a product that is likely to succeed
D. Continuing a product that is likely to succeed
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 7.3. It is natural to drop a concept that would ultimately fail, or continue on a concept that would ultimately succeed. The managerial problem arises when a project that is likely to succeed is discontinued, also referred to as the "drop error." Yet another situation is when a product that is likely to fail is continued. This is called a "go error": A drop error is much worse than a go error and is the costliest.

questions.question: According to the risk/payoff matrix, during the phase of concept/project evaluation of the new products process, a _____ error occurs when a winning product is discarded.
questions.explanation: Refer to figure 7.3. It is natural to drop a concept that would ultimately fail, or continue on a concept that would ultimately succeed. The managerial problem arises when a project that is likely to succeed is discontinued, also referred to as the "drop error."

questions.question: Which of the following risk strategies is most likely to incur opportunity costs?
questions.explanation: In general, the new products team should consider four generic risk strategies. The risk strategy of avoidance eliminates a risky product project altogether, though an opportunity cost is incurred.

questions.question: In which of the following risk strategies is risk reduced to an acceptable, threshold level, perhaps through redesigning a product to include more backup systems or increasing product reliability?
questions.explanation: In general, the new products team should consider four generic risk strategies. Mitigation involves the reduction of risk to an acceptable, threshold level, perhaps through redesigning a product to include more backup systems or increasing product reliability.

questions.question: The use of subcontractors or joint ventures is most likely to be closely associated with the _____ risk strategy.
questions.explanation: The risk strategy of transfer involves moving the responsibility to another organization, in the form of a joint venture or subcontractor, for example. The other party would be better equipped to handle the risk.

questions.question: Which of the following risk strategies typically involves developing a contingency plan to accompany new product development?
questions.explanation: A firm employs the risk strategy of active acceptance by developing a contingency plan to accompany new product development.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of a decay curve?
choices: A. It is primarily a plan rather than a result.
B. It depicts the entire life cycle of product.
C. Decisions on the risk matrix lead to the idea of a decay curve.
D. Synchronization of the two aspects in a decay curve, plan and result, reduces its value as a managerial concept.
questions.explanation: The risk matrix decisions lead to the idea of a decay curve.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the new product evaluation process is untrue?
choices: A. The assumption that a product development plan is mostly tentative.
B. Form and positioning can usually be changed during the process.
C. Everything in new product work should be keyed to a Go/No Go decision.
D. Customer attitudes usually tend to change along the entire process.
questions.explanation: One long-held belief in new product work that is actually untrue is that everything should be keyed to a single Go/No Go decision. One decision can be critical—at times, for example, when a firm must invest millions of dollars in one large facility or when a firm acquires a license that commits it to major financial outlays. But many firms are finding ways to avoid such commitments by transferring risk.

questions.question: A rolling evaluation means that a project is being assessed continuously, which implies that it is dealing with risk via _____.
questions.explanation: Rolling evaluation occurs when a project is being assessed continuously, figures are penciled in, premature closure is avoided, and participants avoid mindsets of good and bad. This is, in a way, dealing with risk via acceptance or mitigation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true of a new product development project that is evaluated with the help of rolling evaluation?
choices: A. The project is assessed at predefined intervals.
B. This evaluation generally leads to the premature closure of a project.
C. Everything in the project is keyed to a single Go/No Go decision.
D. Participants avoid mindsets of good and bad about the project.
questions.explanation: Rolling evaluation occurs when a project is being assessed continuously, figures are penciled in, premature closure is avoided, and participants avoid mindsets of good and bad. This is, in a way, dealing with risk via acceptance or mitigation.

questions.question: The farther a new product idea is allowed to proceed through the development process:
choices: A. lesser the number of people who believe in the concept.
B. the tougher it is to stop the product.
C. the easier it is to wave aside the hurdles.
D. the lesser support it receives from R&D workers.
questions.explanation: Although R&D workers are quite enthusiastic early in the life of a new product, the idea may have little support outside of R&D; it is fragile and easy to kill. Late in the development cycle, more people have bought in on the concept and are supportive because they have played a role in getting it to where it is. Consequently, the now-strong proposal is tough to stop.

questions.question: Concept testing is sometimes called concept _____ to reinforce the idea of helping the item, not just killing it off.
questions.explanation: An evaluation system should contain early testing that is supportive. In fact, concept testing is sometimes called concept development to reinforce the idea of helping the item, not just killing it off.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the people dimension of the evaluation system?
choices: A. It is difficult to kill an idea in the early stage of product development as most of the people are yet to evaluate the idea.
B. Late in the product development cycle, hurdles are usually easy to wave aside.
C. Early in the life of a new product, the product idea may have little support outside of R&D.
D. Late in the product development cycle, fewer people are likely to support the product idea.
questions.explanation: Although R&D workers are quite enthusiastic early in the life of a new product, the idea may have little support outside of R&D; it is fragile and easy to kill. Late in the development cycle, more people have bought in on the concept and are supportive because they have played a role in getting it to where it is. Consequently, the now-strong proposal is tough to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true of surrogate questions?
choices: A. Typically they remain constant at different times in the evaluation process.
B. They are less useful when one wants to gauge customer reactions early on, even before the product is developed.
C. They are based on the fact that the timing of factual information often matches a product developer's need for it.
D. Their response has little value except to help answer a critical question that cannot be answered directly.
questions.explanation: Surrogates often change at different times in the evaluation process. It is important to note that each response to a surrogate question has little value except to help answer a critical question that cannot be answered directly.

questions.question: Lexus Inc. is interested in determining whether a potential new product will be preferred by customers, even before it is launched. Since customer reactions cannot be gauged at this stage, the firm can make use of _____ to gather pieces of information that can substitute for what it wants to learn.
questions.explanation: Lexus Inc. can use surrogate questions to gather information that can substitute for necessary pieces of information. Surrogate questions are useful when one wants to know customer reactions early on, even before a product is developed, if possible. But one can't really know their reactions until one makes some of the product and give it to them to try out. So, one looks for surrogate questions to give pieces of information that can substitute for what one wants to learn but can't.

questions.question: Identify the question that can act as a substitute for the real question, "Will customers prefer the product introduced?" in the product development process.
choices: A. Does the product match the company's manufacturing skills?
B. Will cost of the product be competitive?
C. Did the customers keep the prototype product that was given to them?
D. Will competition leap in once the product is introduced to customers?
questions.explanation: A surrogate question that can act as a substitute for the real question, "Will competition leap in?" is "What did they do last time?"

questions.question: The A-T-A-R model is most akin to a _____.
questions.explanation: The A-T-A-R that is used for designing an evaluation system for each new project as it comes along is based on how we forecast sales and profit on a new item. The calculation is much like a pro forma income statement, an array of figures allowing one to see what the profits will look like based on where one is at any one time in the development.

questions.question: In the case of the A-T-A-R model, R stands for _____.
questions.explanation: In the case of the A-T-A-R model, R stands for repeat. The tool that is used for designing an evaluation system for each new project as it comes along is based on how sales and profit are forecasted on a new item. The basic formula is based on what is known in the marketing field as the A-T-A-R concept (awareness-trial-availability-repeat).

questions.question: The A-T-A-R concept is taken from _____.
questions.explanation: The A-T-A-R Model is taken from what is called diffusion of innovation, explained this way: For a person or a firm to become a regular buyer/user of an innovation, there must first be awareness that it exists, then there must be a decision to try that innovation, then the person must find the item available to them, and finally there must be the type of happiness with it that leads to adoption, or repeat usage.

questions.question: VSFS Software Solutions Inc. is aware that its newly launched app is prone to certain risks and creates a contingency plan to counter the risk. Which generic risk strategy is the company adopting in this scenario?
questions.explanation: In general, the new products team should consider four generic risk strategies: avoidance, mitigation, transfer, and acceptance. Acceptance involves developing a contingency plan now (active acceptance) or dealing with the risks as they come up (passive acceptance).

questions.question: In the context of the A-T-A-R model, _____ means the percentage chance that if a buyer wants to try a product, the effort to find it will be successful.
questions.explanation: "Available" means the percentage chance that if a buyer wants to try a product, the effort to find it will be successful; this is often the "percent of stores that stock it." Direct sellers have 100 percent availability.

questions.question: In the context of the A-T-A-R model, _____ means someone in the buying unit hears about the existence of a new product with some characteristic that differentiates it.
questions.explanation: "Aware" means someone in the buying unit hears about the existence of a new product with some characteristic that differentiates it; this is subject to variation between industries and even between developers.

questions.question: While preparing the product innovation charter (PIC), the earliest evaluation that a firm makes is of ____.
choices: B. the legal requirements it has to fulfill
C. the technologies used by its competitors
questions.explanation: The Product Innovation Charter is the earliest evaluation that a firm makes of itself and its situation. That evaluation yields "a priori" conclusions about new product proposals. The firm reaches these conclusions while making basic strategic decisions on the product innovation charter.
questions.topic: Concept Evaluation: Fit with Product Innovation Charter

questions.question: Which of the following is true of the product innovation charter (PIC) of a firm?
choices: A. The PIC is formulated at the end of the new products process.
B. The formulation of the PIC follows the phase of opportunity identification and concept generation.
C. The PIC precludes the practice of having unwanted proposals eat up valuable development funds before they are detected.
D. The PIC tends to eliminate less product ideas than any of the other evaluation techniques.
questions.explanation: The PIC given to new products management eliminates more product ideas than all the other evaluations combined. By coming at the beginning of the new products system, it precludes the unfortunate practice of having unwanted proposals eat up valuable development funds before they are detected.
questions.topic: Concept Evaluation: Fit with Product Innovation Charter

questions.question: Concept testing will work best for:
choices: A. concepts related to consumer packaged goods.
B. concepts embodying new art and entertainment.
C. concepts embodying some new technology that users cannot visualize.
D. concepts related to a product whose prime benefit is a personal sense.
questions.explanation: Most major firms make frequent use of concept testing. It is a mandatory part of the process for makers of consumer packaged goods. And use is growing in industrial firms, which actually invented it. Business-to-business firms have always spent much time talking with users about their needs and problems, what suggestions they have, what they think about various ideas, and so on. They just never called it concept testing.

questions.question: Concept testing was essentially invented by ____.
questions.explanation: The use of concept testing is growing in industrial firms, which actually invented it. Most major firms make frequent use of concept testing. It is a mandatory part of the process for makers of consumer packaged goods.

questions.question: If it is simple to go from concept to full service description, then the services firm can proceed to:
choices: A. developing the product innovation charter.
questions.explanation: If it is simple to go from concept to full service description (a form of prototype), then the services firm can proceed to what is called prototype concept testing. Such testing is, of course, much more reliable with a physical prototype to talk around.

questions.question: A product concept is a:
choices: A. finalized result of core competency.
D. claim of proposed value to customers.
questions.explanation: A new product concept is a stated relationship between product features (form or technology) and consumer benefits (needs satisfied). That is, the product concept is a claim of proposed value to the customer.

questions.question: Concept testing is a part of the _____ process.
questions.explanation: Concept testing is part of the prescreening process, preparing a management team to do the full screening of the idea by providing input into the full screen just before beginning serious technical work. Screeners use scoring models and write out product protocols.

questions.question: The first purpose of concept testing is to:
choices: A. estimate the likely sales or trial rate.
B. identify very poor concepts for early elimination.
C. refine revenue estimates claimed by marketers.
D. identify the technology needed for development.
questions.explanation: The first purpose of a concept test is to identify the very poor concept so it can be eliminated. If music lovers, for example, don't care about a new kind of compact disc that will last forever (because they download all their music from online sources) and thus reject it out of hand, the concept is probably a poor one.

questions.question: Once a concept passes the first hurdle, concept testing will focus next on:
choices: A. estimating the product's sales or trial rate.
questions.explanation: If a concept passes the first hurdle, a second purpose is to estimate, even crudely, the sales or trial rate that the product would enjoy—a sense of market share or a general range of revenue dollars. A prediction based on purchase intention can be a rough but good indication of future sales and can be used to assess the worthiness of the product concept.

questions.question: According to the classic five-point question format of the concept test for a product, the top-two-boxes score includes the number of people who:
choices: A. definitely would buy the product or probably would buy the product.
B. probably would buy the product or might or might not buy the product.
C. might or might not buy the product or probably would not buy the product.
D. probably would buy the product or definitely would not buy the product.
questions.explanation: The number or percentage of people who definitely would buy or probably would buy the product, usually combined and used as an indicator of group reaction, is called the top-two-boxes score, as it refers to the total number of times one of the top two boxes on the questionnaire (definitely or probably) were checked.

questions.question: According to the classic five-point question format for purchase intentions, which of the following is true of the top-two-boxes score?
choices: A. This score represents the number or percentage of people who definitely would not buy a product.
B. This score is used as an indicator of group reaction.
C. Researchers who calibrate this score believe that it reflects real figures.
D. This score is used to indicate the number or percentage of people who might or might not buy a product.
questions.explanation: According to the classic five-point question format for purchase intentions, the number or percentage of people who definitely would buy or probably would buy the product are usually combined and used as an indicator of group reaction. This is called the top-two-boxes score, as it is the total number of times one of the top two boxes on the questionnaire (definitely or probably) were checked.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest supplier of concept tests?
questions.explanation: The BASES Group, the largest supplier of concept tests and now part of A. C. Nielsen, has data banks that literally let a client company calibrate all of its concept test questions by product type.

questions.question: A concept statement developed during the new product development process:
choices: A. describes the technology to be used for manufacturing the product.
B. discusses the results of prototype testing.
C. states a difference and how that difference benefits the customer.
D. lists the guidelines for developing the new product.
questions.explanation: A concept statement states a difference and how that difference benefits the customer or end user.

questions.question: Practitioners urge that a concept statement should:
choices: B. always be presented to potential buyers in a verbal format.
C. be as descriptive and lengthy as possible.
D. relate in some way to things familiar to the customer.
questions.explanation: Practitioners urge that any concept statement should make the new item's difference absolutely clear, claim determinant attributes (those that make a difference in buying decisions), offer an element of familiarity by relating in some way to things familiar to the customer, and be completely credible and realistic. And short, as short as possible, although there have been concept statements of 3-5 pages that worked very well in complex technical situations.

questions.question: Which of the following has to be usually supplemented by a narrative statement of the concept in a concept statement?
questions.explanation: Drawings, diagrams, and sketches comprise a second way to present concepts to respondents. Visuals, like diagrams and sketches, must be supplemented by a narrative statement of the concept.

questions.question: A commercialized concept statement:
choices: A. sounds more like how a product would actually be promoted or advertised to customers.
B. does not produce realistic customer evaluations.
C. is also known as a "stripped description."
D. just presents facts in the form of bullet points.
questions.explanation: A commercialized concept statement is an embellished description that sounds more like how a product would actually be promoted or advertised to customers. A noncommercialized concept statement, on the other hand, presents just the facts (this can even be in bullet points).

questions.question: Which of the following formats of concept testing produces more realistic evaluations but also risks the bias of good or poor advertising copy writing?
questions.explanation: Due to their similarity to advertising copy, some say that commercialized statements will produce more realistic customer evaluations (that is, greater acceptance); nevertheless, good or poor advertising copywriting might bias the results.

questions.question: Which of the following adopter groups are the most important for concept testing of new products and, probably, market acceptance?
choices: A. Early majority and late majority
questions.explanation: Some new products people, aware that they will first have to interest the innovators and early adopters in a market, concentrate their concept testing solely on them. If this group is interested, it's a good bet others will be also.

questions.question: Which of the following is an immediate and critical question in concept testing that should be answered prior to all other questions?
choices: A. How likely is it that the respondents would buy the product?
B. How much do the respondents like the concept?
C. Does the respondent understand the concept?
D. What are the respondents' reactions to price?
questions.explanation: Background information helps one understand and interpret comments about the new concept, which are asked for next. The immediate and critical question is, "Does the respondent understand the concept?" Given understanding, one then seeks other reactions.

questions.question: Track Inc. seeks to identify unsatisfied market segments in the health care insurance segment. It wants to concentrate its efforts on developing concepts ideally suited to the needs of these segments. For this purpose, the firm is most likely to employ _____.
choices: B. a risk or payoff matrix
questions.explanation: Track Inc. is most likely to employ benefit segmentation. Through benefit segmentation, a firm may identify unsatisfied market segments and concentrate its efforts on developing concepts ideally suited to the needs of these segments.

questions.question: The benefit segments overlaid onto a perceptual map result in a ____, which allows assessment of the preferences of each benefit segment for different product concepts.
questions.explanation: One can overlay benefit segments onto a perceptual map. The result is called a joint space map, and it allows one to assess the preferences of each benefit segment for different product concepts. Joint space maps can be developed using ideal brand ratings or preference regression.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of conjoint analysis in concept testing?
choices: A. Conjoint analysis cannot feasibly test attributes and levels using a reduced set of cards.
B. Conjoint analysis ranks the possible combinations of attributes from the least preferred to the most preferred.
C. Conjoint analysis cannot be used to identify those concepts that are the "real losers," which should not be considered for further development.
D. Conjoint analysis is extremely useful in concept testing because of its ability to uncover relationships between attributes and customer preferences.
questions.explanation: Conjoint analysis is extremely useful in concept testing because of its ability to uncover relationships between attributes (features, functions, benefits) and customer preferences.

questions.question: Conjoint analysis is used to identify _____.
choices: B. the optimum combination of attributes
D. the optimum price for a product
questions.explanation: Conjoint analysis is used identify high-potential gaps: combinations of attributes that (a) customers like and (b) are not on the market yet.

questions.question: In the context of concept statements, a(n) _____ description presents just the facts (this can even be in bullet points), whereas a(n) _____ description sounds more like how the product would actually be promoted or advertised to customers.
questions.explanation: A noncommercialized concept statement or a stripped description presents just the facts. A commercialized concept statement or an embellished description sounds more like how the product would actually be promoted or advertised to customers.

questions.question: Even if a product's potential is extremely high, its sales may not materialize due to insufficient marketing effort.
questions.explanation: A product's potential may be extremely high, but sales may not materialize due to insufficient marketing effort. This is one of the several guidelines that have to be kept in mind when developing sales forecasts.

questions.question: In a new product development process, the financial analysis generally begins with the calculation of the net present value, NPV.
questions.explanation: In the new product development process, the financial analysis generally begins with sales forecasts. Once sales have been projected over the next several planning periods, assessment of costs, projection of profits, and calculation of key financial benchmarks such as net present value or internal rate of return can be done.

questions.question: In the product development process, sales forecasting is typically the responsibility of the process manager on the new product team.
questions.explanation: In the new product development process, sales forecasting is typically the responsibility of the marketing person on the new product team. Once sales have been projected over the next several planning periods, assessment of costs, projection of profits, and calculation of key financial benchmarks such as net present value or internal rate of return can be done.

questions.question: In addition to the considerations of time and cost, one should also consider product and market newness when selecting the most appropriate forecasting model.
questions.explanation: In addition to the considerations of time and cost, one should also consider product and market newness when selecting the most appropriate forecasting model. The most straightforward kind of forecast to conduct is a sales analysis, used for current technologies being sold into current markets.

questions.question: The A-T-A-R model is one of the pseudo sale market testing methods used later in the new product process, typically when the physical product is available for the consumer to take home and try.
questions.explanation: The A-T-A-R model is one of the pseudo sale market testing methods used later in the new product process, typically when the physical product is available for the consumer to take home and try. Post-trial data are then collected from the consumer and used as input to the A-T-A-R model.
questions.topic: Forecasting Sales Using the A-T-A-R Model

questions.question: Laggards refer to those users who will be among the first to try the product.
questions.explanation: Early adopters refer to those users who will be among the first to try the product. In theory, individuals in the earlier adopter categories influence the purchase behaviors of later ones through word of mouth and other influence processes.

questions.question: Adoption of innovation refers to the process by which an innovation is spread within a market, over time and over categories of adopters.
questions.explanation: Diffusion of innovation refers to the process by which an innovation is spread within a market, over time and over categories of adopters. The rate of diffusion of a product can be difficult to assess, especially at an early stage in a new product process, since it is unknown how influential the earlier adopter categories will ultimately be.

questions.question: Product innovators outside of consumer packaged goods still most often use the simple version of the A-T-A-R model.
questions.explanation: Product innovators outside of consumer packaged goods still most often use the simple version of the A-T-A-R model. The A-T-A-R model is one of the pseudo sale market testing methods used later in the new product process, typically when the physical product is available for the consumer to take home and try.

questions.question: Most common forecasting methods are extrapolations and work well on established products.
questions.explanation: Most common forecasting methods are extrapolations and work well on established products. New products don't have a history to be extrapolated.

questions.question: An early field use test with a prototype will not assure success, but it can say intended users like what they see.
questions.explanation: An early field use test with a prototype won't assure success, but it can say intended users like what they see. An advertising agency or a sales manager cannot guarantee success either, but they can assess whether the new item will be brought to the attention of potential end-users and that it will be tried.
questions.topic: Actions by Managers to Handle These Problems

questions.question: Factor analysis can be used to estimate the net present value of a new product when it is still in the concept stage.
questions.explanation: Real-options analysis may be used to estimate the net present value of a new product when it is still in the concept stage. It accounts for the fact that there still are unknowns at this early stage, and that the firm may need to abandon the project at some time in the future as more information is obtained, and uncertainty is reduced.
questions.topic: Actions by Managers to Handle These Problems

questions.question: Many of the mathematical sales forecasting models were initially developed for use on durable goods.
questions.explanation: Many of the mathematical sales forecasting models were initially developed for non-durable goods. However, efforts continue to make them work better on durable goods.
questions.topic: Actions by Managers to Solve These Problems

questions.question: New product projects need to be considered on how well they fit a firm's strategy for innovation.
questions.explanation: New product projects need to be considered on how well they fit the firm's strategy for innovation. Many firms report that too many new product projects get approved, and the human and financial resources end up getting spread too thin.

questions.question: In a bottom-up strategic approach, the firm lays out its strategy first, and then allocates funds across different kinds of projects.
questions.explanation: In a bottom-up approach to strategy development, strategic criteria are built into a firm's project selection tools. In a top-down strategic approach, a firm lays out its strategy first, and then allocates funds across different kinds of projects.

questions.question: With reference to new product development, the top performing firms tend to rely only on financial criteria.
questions.explanation: The top-performing firms often use a combination of top-down and bottom-up approaches and consider strategic as well as financial criteria when selecting projects, while the worst performers tend to rely only on financial criteria.

questions.question: Which of the following is a consideration to keep in mind when developing a sales forecast?
choices: A. Advertising may not adequately create awareness.
B. Sales will usually not grow through time even if customers get to try the product.
C. A product's sales do not depend on competitors' strategies.
D. Regardless of the marketing effort, a product's sales will materialize if the product's potential is extremely high.
questions.explanation: Several considerations should be kept in mind when developing a sales forecast. First, a product's potential may be extremely high, but sales may not materialize because of insufficient marketing effort. Advertising may not adequately create awareness, or inadequate distribution may make the product unavailable to much of the market.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of sales forecasting for new products?
choices: A. If a product's potential is high, sales will materialize in spite of insufficient marketing efforts.
B. Sales forecasting is the final step in a financial analysis.
C. Sales forecasting is conducted only after calculating key financial benchmarks such as net present value or internal rate of return.
D. Sales forecasting is typically the responsibility of the marketing personnel on the new products team.
questions.explanation: The financial analysis begins with the sales forecast. This is typically the responsibility of the marketing person on the new product team. Once sales have been projected over the next several planning periods, one can assess costs, make profit projections, and calculate key financial benchmarks such as net present value or internal rate of return.

questions.question: Sales forecasting is typically the responsibility of a _____ on a new product team.
questions.explanation: Sales forecasting is typically the responsibility of a marketing person on a new product team. Other participants on the team (such as manufacturing engineers, R&D people, financial and accounting specialists, etc.) have a greater input in providing the costs and other data that will make up the financial analysis.

questions.question: In a new product development process, which of the following is most likely to be determined first while analyzing the financial aspects of a product?
questions.explanation: In a new product development process, sales forecast is most likely to be determined first while analyzing the financial aspects of a product. Sales forecast is typically the responsibility of the marketing person of a new product team.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most straightforward kind of new product forecast to conduct?
questions.explanation: In addition to the considerations of time and cost, one should also consider product and market newness when selecting the most appropriate forecasting model. The most straightforward kind of forecast to conduct is a sales analysis, used for current technologies being sold into current markets.

questions.question: Ancon Inc., typically forecasts potential product sales based on the number of customers who say they would either definitely or probably buy the product, on a five-point scale. The firm's sales forecast is based upon _____.
questions.explanation: Purchase intentions generally make use of a five-point scale. This helps in realizing the customers' likelihood of purchasing a product if it was made available.

questions.question: _____ is one of the pseudo sale market testing methods used later in the new product process, typically when the physical product is available for the consumer to take home and try.
questions.explanation: The A-T-A-R model is one of the pseudo sale market testing methods used later in the new product process, typically when the physical product is available for the consumer to take home and try. Post-trial data are then collected from the consumer and used as input to the A-T-A-R model.
